_note: Editorial definition of the replay 'Rome's wars'. Events come from the key-events snapshot (wikidata-events.json, at least 12 Wikipedia editions); tools/fetch_replay.py adds what Wikidata says each is part of (P361) and who took part (P710). An event belongs to the replay when Rome took part in it or in a conflict it is part of (P361, followed upwards), or when such a conflict is one of the anchors. 'add' and 'drop' correct Wikidata where it is silent or too broad; each says why, with a quotation from the stored Wikipedia text (data/stories/en) or the item's Wikidata description, checked by tools/build_replay.py.

anchors.label: list of Roman civil wars and revolts
anchors.why: Wikidata files the civil wars (Sulla, Caesar, the Liberators, Actium) as part of this list; their participants are Roman factions, not Rome.

anchors.label: Crisis of the Roman Republic
anchors.why: Parent of the Sertorian War, whose participants are Roman factions and their allies.

anchors.label: Wars of Augustus
anchors.why: Parent of Octavian's wars (Mutina, Perusia, Sicily, the final war).

anchors.label: Roman conquest of Hispania
anchors.why: Parent of the Celtiberian and Lusitanian wars.

anchors.label: Roman conquest of Britain
anchors.why: Parent of Caesar's invasions of Britain.

add.label: Jugurthine War
add.quote: war between Kingdom of Numidia and the Roman Republic
add.why: Wikidata gives it no participants and no 'part of'; its description names the two sides.

add.label: Crossing the Rubicon
add.quote: crossing of the Rubicon river by Julius Caesar in January 49 BC
add.why: The act that began Caesar's Civil War; Wikidata links it to no war.

add.label: Treaty of Apamea
add.quote: between the Roman Republic and Antiochus III
add.why: Ended the Roman–Seleucid War; Wikidata links it to no war.

add.label: Treaty of Dardanos
add.why: Ended the First Mithridatic War; Wikidata links it to no war.

drop.label: Mercenary War
drop.quote: a mutiny by troops that were employed by Carthage
drop.why: Wikidata files it under the Punic Wars, but Rome took no part.

drop.label: Battle of the Saw
drop.quote: between a Carthaginian army led by Hamilcar Barca and a rebel force
drop.why: A battle of the Mercenary War.

drop.label: Battle of Mantinea (207 BC)
drop.quote: between Sparta under the tyrant Machanidas
drop.why: Part of the First Macedonian War on Wikidata, fought between Greek leagues without Rome.
